paras: The threatened lynching of Ben Rushing took place at James Bayou, Missouri, after Rushing was accused of shooting J. B. Lindsey dead there on Christmas Day, December 25, 1882. A wire dispatch from Cairo, Illinois, reported that the accused man was in the hands of a mob and that lynching was expected, but the Cairo Bulletin later reported that he had been captured and jailed at Charleston, Missouri. No report gives the race of either man.

According to the Daily Cairo Bulletin, Rushing shot Lindsey during a quarrel because Lindsey had thrown a glass of whisky in his face. The wire versions spelled the dead man's name "Lindsley", while the Bulletin and some other papers used "Lindsey".

A Cairo special to the Cincinnati Commercial, dated December 26, said that Lindsey had been shot dead the day before at James Bayou. It added that "when the steamer Tyler left his murderer was in the hands of the mob and lynching was expected," without naming the accused man or describing the mob. The news reached Cairo with the departure of the steamer Tyler, and the coverage gives no later word from James Bayou itself about what the mob did.
On December 31 the Cairo Bulletin reported that Rushing "has been captured, and is in jail at Charleston, Mo." No report of an inquest, indictment or trial appears in the coverage.

The Cairo item ran on December 27 and 28 in papers from Washington and Lancaster to Memphis, Omaha, Salt Lake City and Sacramento, nearly always as one sentence in a roundup of Christmas shootings, stabbings and suicides. The National Republican placed it under the headline "Terrible Tragedies, Principally in the South," and the Memphis Daily Appeal among its "Wire Waifs." The Omaha Daily Bee headed the item "Speedy Justice," treating the expected lynching as summary punishment.

The Daily Leader shortened the wire to say flatly that the murderer "is in the hands of a mob and lynching is expected." On December 30 the Fremont County Record of Canon City, Colorado, listed the case among "Christmas Crimes" and went further, writing that "it is believed his murderer was hanged." Only the Cairo Bulletin, published near the scene, followed the story to Rushing's arrest, and none of the coverage identifies anyone by race.

Accounts of Rushing's fate differ: the wire left him in a mob's hands with lynching expected, a Colorado weekly said he was believed hanged, and the Cairo Bulletin said he was in jail at Charleston. The Bulletin's report is the latest, the most local and the only one to name him, while the Colorado claim of a hanging appears to rest on the wire's expectation of one.

A mob held the man accused of shooting Lindsey with lynching expected (A1, A6), but the latest and most local report says Ben Rushing was captured and jailed at Charleston, Mo. (A12); only a Colorado roundup said it was 'believed' he was hanged (A11).

Every report of the mob and the expected lynching goes back to one Cairo special to the Cincinnati Commercial (A1, A2, A3, A6); the Cairo Bulletin independently confirms the shooting and the capture but not the mob (A12).
